page: Microsoft Azure L32aos_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine powered by the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 3.7 GHz, supported by 256.0 GB of system memory (8.0 GB per vCPU) and a 32 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 23,040 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and operates under Microsoft Hyper-V. The CPU includes vector and cryptographic instruction sets, such as AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, while omitting discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-core CPU throughput, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring 3077.95 and Geekbench single-core reaching 2085.0, both placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is balanced, with Geekbench multi-core at 17812.0 and PassMark CPU score at 46529.17. High cryptographic throughput is evidenced by a PassMark encryption score of 38579.19. Memory bandwidth reaches 73.38 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 55.9 GB/sec for uncached writes, while Redis operations clock at 46.17 million operations per second.

With a massive 23,040 GB NVMe SSD allocation and an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the instance is architected for low-latency, high-IOPS applications that require rapid access to dense local storage. Tradeoffs include standard multi-threaded CPU efficiency alongside the absence of dedicated hardware accelerators. The instance profile is suited for large relational and NoSQL databases, search indexing engines, real-time analytics, and data-intensive distributed file systems.

The AMD processor includes AVX-512 and hardware cryptographic instructions. Benchmark assessments show top-quartile single-core CPU execution, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2085.0 and stress-ng score of 3077.95, accompanied by strong encryption throughput. The balanced combination of dense local NVMe storage and substantial memory capacity delivers a solid configuration for I/O-intensive workloads, including high-scale transactional databases, distributed storage clusters, and analytical data stores, without relying on external accelerators.
